key_insight: Conditioning recurrent forecasts on temperature and thermal rate enables accurate prediction of grain growth during non-isothermal heat treatment.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a computationally efficient alternative to repeated grain-growth simulations for exploring heat-treatment schedules.
method: Encode grain size distributions with a convolutional neural network.
Embed instantaneous temperature and thermal rate with a dedicated multilayer perceptron.
Forecast microstructural evolution with a thermally conditioned recurrent network.
evidence_signal: On front-tracking simulation data, k-fold cross-validation yielded mean relative errors of 2.99% for one-hour cycles and 4.51% for four-hour cycles, with R² above 0.99; errors ranged from 1.91% to 14.66% across ten simulations with four unseen thermal histories.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-based, and the higher errors on some unseen thermal histories warrant caution when extrapolating to new heat-treatment conditions.
paper_title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
